candidates.attacker_control: The text passed to `StringSubstitutor.replace(...)`/`replaceIn(...)`/`replaceIn(StringBuilder)` by the host application (request parameters, headers, config values, templates, log or message content). The lookup prefix and its key (`engineName` + script body) are taken verbatim from the `${...}` expression, e.g. `${script:javascript:<payload>}`, `${url:UTF-8:http://<internal-host>}`, `${file:UTF-8:/etc/passwd}`, `${dns:address|<host>}`.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that this is not merely an advertised opt-in feature: the enum is iterated unfiltered at StringLookupFactory.java:411-414, and InterpolatorStringLookup.java:101 hard-codes addDefaultLookups=true, so there is no allowlist or switch that excludes `script` in this version; the class javadoc (StringLookupFactory.java:43-155) and the createInterpolator example (StringSubstitutor.java:291-296) explicitly present `${script:...}` as part of the default interpolator, with no warning not to use untrusted input (the constant-time factory methods at 407-416 and the singleton at InterpolatorStringLookup.java:37 make this the stock behavior). Checked that the plain `new StringSubstitutor(Map)` / static replace paths use `mapStringLookup` only (StringSubstitutor.java:421-434) and are not affected, so the finding is scoped to the interpolator factories rather than the whole class. Verified `resolveVariable` has no sanitization step (1061-1068) and that the lookup key reaches eval unchanged.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary code execution inside the host JVM with the application's privileges via the `script` lookup (script engine evaluation of attacker-supplied code, e.g. JavaScript/Groovy expressions able to invoke Java APIs); server-side request forgery and local file disclosure via `${url:UTF-8:file:///...}` / `${file:...}` / `${url:...}`; DNS-based exfiltration via `${dns:...}`; and disclosure of environment variables, system properties and bundles via `${env:...}`/`${sys:...}`/`${properties:...}`/`${resourceBundle:...}`. A single interpolation token in attacker-controlled text is sufficient once the vulnerable factory is adopted.
candidates.prerequisites: Host application integrates the interpolator (`StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator()` or `StringLookupFactory.INSTANCE.interpolatorStringLookup()`) and substitutes text containing attacker-influenced segments. For the script vector, a JSR-223 engine matching the supplied name must be on the classpath (JavaScript/Nashorn ships with Java 8-14, the JDK level this release targets; Groovy/other engines if present). The url/file/dns/env/sys vectors need only the JDK. No non-default flags are required: single-level `${...}` variables are resolved with stock settings (`enableSubstitutionInVariables` is not needed).
candidates.root_cause: `DefaultStringLookup` still contains SCRIPT (88-91), DNS (51-56) and URL (98-101) in 1.9, and `StringLookupFactory.addDefaultStringLookups` (407-416) blindly registers every enum constant into the interpolator map. `InterpolatorStringLookup`'s constructor path ends at line 100-102, which hard-codes `addDefaultLookups=true`, so no opt-in is required. Consequently `StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator()` returns a substitutor whose lookup map resolves the `script` prefix to `ScriptStringLookup`, which evaluates the embedded text with a JSR-223 engine. There is no allowlist, no trust-boundary check, and no warning in this version that untrusted text must never be substituted.
candidates.title: Default string-lookup set in StringSubstitutor interpolator exposes `script` (and `url`/`file`/`dns`) on attacker-controlled input, enabling code execution, SSRF and file disclosure
candidates.trace: createInterpolator (StringSubstitutor.java:303-305) -> StringLookupFactory.interpolatorStringLookup (StringLookupFactory.java:706-708) -> InterpolatorStringLookup.INSTANCE (InterpolatorStringLookup.java:37) -> ctor chain 58-60 / 91-93 / 100-102 with addDefaultLookups=true -> StringLookupFactory.addDefaultStringLookups (407-416) iterates DefaultStringLookup.values(), registering key `script` -> ScriptStringLookup.INSTANCE. At substitution time, the default `${`/`}` scan (StringSubstitutor.substitute, 1323-1448) extracts the variable name and calls resolveVariable (1061-1068) -> InterpolatorStringLookup.lookup (122-147) splits at the first `:` and dispatches prefix `script` -> ScriptStringLookup.lookup (68-91): `new ScriptEngineManager().getEngineByName(engineName)` (line 82) followed by `scriptEngine.eval(script)` (line 86). The javadoc table at StringLookupFactory.java:43-155 confirms script/url/dns/file are advertised default lookups.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: no code was executed. Exploitability depends on host-application integration (whether untrusted text is passed to an interpolator-configured substitutor), which is outside this library snapshot, and on a JSR-223 engine being present for the script vector (Nashorn is bundled in Java 8-14 — the release targets Java 8 — but removed in Java 15+; the url/file/dns vectors are JDK-only and remain). The P1 index implements no data-flow/control-flow analysis and reports 1641 unresolved call sites, so the chain above is argued from source text and navigation edges, not from a proven data flow.
candidates.weakness_type: Code injection / insecure default configuration (CWE-94, CWE-1188; same root cause also yields CWE-918/CWE-22)

coverage_summary: Scope: 125 files (100 Java, 25 non-Java: pom/build, site docs, workflows, checkstyle). The P1 index parsed all 100 Java files with 0 omissions/mismatches, but implements no control-flow/data-flow/semantic resolution and leaves 1641 calls unresolved. No test sources are present in the snapshot. Deep review: the entire lookup package (ScriptStringLookup, InterpolatorStringLookup, DefaultStringLookup, StringLookupFactory, Url/File/Dns/Constant/Properties/ResourceBundle lookups), the StringSubstitutor substitution core (substitute/resolveVariable/createInterpolator/defaults), and StringSubstitutorReader. Targeted repository-wide greps for Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder, ScriptEngine/eval, URL construction, ObjectInputStream and Class.forName. Sampling review: StringEscapeUtils, translate package, WordUtils, StrBuilder/TextStringBuilder hot spots, NumericEntityUnescaper, LookupTranslator. Not exhaustively line-reviewed: similarity/diff packages, ExtendedMessageFormat, AlphabetConverter, RandomStringGenerator, StringTokenizer and the full bodies of the two large builders.
limitations: No code, tests or scanners were executed; the finding is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

The vulnerable behavior is a library default; concrete exploitability depends on an external host application adopting StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator() (or interpolatorStringLookup()) and passing untrusted text to it — that integration is not present or verifiable in this snapshot.

Script execution requires a matching JSR-223 engine on the deployment classpath (JavaScript/Nashorn in Java 8-14; removed in Java 15+), so the script vector is environment-dependent, while url/file/dns vectors are JDK-only.
P1 index limitations: no data-flow or control-flow, no semantic resolution, 1641 unresolved calls; index edges are syntactic candidates only.
No test sources exist in the snapshot, so validation against tests was not possible.
Several large utility classes were only sampled, not read exhaustively.

summary: Apache Commons Text 1.9 snapshot. The strongest source-supported issue is an unsafe default configuration in the string-interpolation subsystem: `StringSubstitutor.createInterpolator()` wires `InterpolatorStringLookup` with `StringLookupFactory.addDefaultStringLookups`, which registers every `DefaultStringLookup` constant — including `script`, `url`, `dns` and `file`. No allowlist, opt-in or warning exists in this version. Input containing `${script:<engine>:<code>}` that reaches `replace()` is passed verbatim to `ScriptStringLookup.lookup`, which obtains a JSR-223 engine and calls `eval()` — i.e., attacker-controlled code execution in any host application that interpolates untrusted text. The same default set enables SSRF/local file read (`url`, `file`), DNS exfiltration (`dns`) and env/sys/properties disclosure. Plain map-based substitution is unaffected; the flaw is specific to the documented interpolator factories.
